correctness.rationale: Haar difference of two independent torus points is Haar; its centered Voronoi representative is area-uniform and distance equals radial norm. The Gauss-reduced rank-two lattice Voronoi cell has two or three opposite facet pairs and all vertices on one centered circumcircle: disk intersection is pi t² minus two disjoint circular caps for each distance d_i. A cap begins at d_i with positive coefficient 4sqrt(2d_i)/3 h^(3/2), and earlier caps remain analytic, so the full CDF identifies area and every facet threshold with multiplicity. Rectangle sides or SSS Delaunay triangle then reconstruct the generating lattice, including repeated-distance degeneracies. Separate angular half-plane integration matches cap formulas in 12 parameter/radius cases.

value.rationale: Constructive inverse metric rigidity from a one-dimensional, unoriented and unlabeled population distance law is a natural strong identifiability problem. The proof handles every planar lattice, including rectangular and symmetric degeneracies, not an artificial finite slice.

final_claim: Exact Haar pair geodesic distance distribution of every flat Euclidean 2-torus is circular-cap CDF of a cyclic Voronoi rectangle/hexagon, whose 3/2 singular onsets recover its facet-distance multiset and hence the lattice up to isometry including scale.
limitations: Euclidean flat 2-tori only, intrinsic geodesic distance, exact Haar population CDF; no finite-sample robustness or higher-dimensional assertion.
